questions.scenario: A transfer fee method has a `switch` with a case per channel, and product managers add a channel every quarter.
questions.question: Which refactoring best fits?
options: Singleton: make the fee method static
Decorator: wrap the switch in another switch
Strategy: one FeeRule implementation per channel, collected by a calculator, so a new channel adds a class instead of editing the switch
Observer: publish an event for every fee
questions.explanation: Strategy keeps the calculator closed for modification and open for extension; Spring can inject all FeeRule beans as a list.

questions.scenario: A service has a `@Transactional` method `transferAll()` that loops and calls `this.transferOne()`, also `@Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW)`. Each transfer was expected to commit separately, but they all roll back together.
questions.question: Why?
options: REQUIRES_NEW is not supported by PostgreSQL
Loops can't run inside transactions
Calls through `this` bypass the Spring proxy, so `transferOne()`'s transaction settings are never applied
Spring creates a new proxy for every loop iteration
questions.explanation: Spring applies @Transactional through a proxy around the bean. Self-invocation doesn't pass through the proxy; move transferOne() to another bean or use TransactionTemplate.

questions.scenario: A `QuoteService` Spring bean stores `private BigDecimal lastRate` and sets it during each request. Customers occasionally see someone else's rate.
questions.question: What is the cause?
options: BigDecimal is not thread-safe for reading
Spring creates one bean per HTTP session by default
The JVM caches the field per user
Beans are singletons by default and shared by all request threads, so the field is shared mutable state
questions.explanation: Singleton beans must be stateless or hold only thread-safe, immutable state. Keep per-request values in local variables or parameters.

questions.scenario: After a transfer commits, the bank must send an SMS, update a fraud score and refresh a dashboard, and new reactions are added often.
questions.question: Which approach keeps the transfer service decoupled and safe?
options: Use @EventListener so listeners run inside the transaction
Make the transfer service extend the SMS service
Publish a TransferCompleted application event and handle it with @TransactionalEventListener, which runs after commit
Call the three services directly at the start of the method
questions.explanation: Observer via events decouples the publisher; the transactional listener avoids notifying about transfers that roll back.

questions.scenario: Your code calls a KYC vendor whose SDK returns `VendorVerificationResponseV3` objects, and these types appear in controllers and repositories.
questions.question: What should you introduce?
options: A Builder for the vendor response
An Adapter implementing your own KycProvider interface that translates the vendor's types into your domain types
A Singleton wrapper around the SDK
A Template Method in the controller
questions.explanation: Adapters keep third-party types at the edge, so switching vendors touches one class.

questions.scenario: Which of these are examples of the Template Method idea (a fixed algorithm with variable steps) in Spring? (Choose two.)
questions.question: Select two.
options: JdbcTemplate.query(sql, rowMapper)
@Value("${app.limit}")
TransactionTemplate.execute(status -> ...)
A record with a compact constructor
questions.explanation: Both templates run fixed steps (resources, exceptions, commit/rollback) and call your callback for the variable part.

questions.scenario: A record `Transfer` has nine components, four of them Strings, and tests keep passing arguments in the wrong order.
questions.question: What improves construction most?
options: Use a Map<String, Object> instead of a record
A Builder (hand-written or generated) or static factory methods with named steps, validating in build()
Make all fields public and mutable
Add a no-argument constructor and setters
questions.explanation: Builders make many-argument construction readable and checkable while keeping the object immutable.

questions.scenario: A teammate adds an interface plus a factory for a class that has one implementation, no test double and no planned alternatives.
questions.question: What is the best review comment?
options: Approve, more interfaces are always better
Ask them to add an abstract base class as well
Ask for a Singleton too
Suggest removing the speculative abstraction until a second implementation or test need appears
questions.explanation: Patterns add indirection; introduce them when they solve a present problem.
